newsitem.title: UK: Hiscox says end Lloyd's annual venture.
newsitem.headline: Hiscox says end Lloyd's annual venture.

text.p: A leading figure at Lloyd's of London on Tuesday called for the capital structure of the insurance market to be simplified.
Robert Hiscox, chairman of insurance group Hiscox Plc, described the annual venture - where Lloyd's traditional backers, Names, reform syndicates anew each year - as an "anachronistic absurdity".
The current mixture of unlimited and limited liability Names was too expensive to maintain, he said.
"With all underwriting capital and management integrated in corporate structures, the cost of regulation could be vastly reduced," said Hiscox.

"The abolition of the annual venture would make redundant the extraordinary accounting procedures in the maintenance of separate solvency statistics and accounts for thousands of individual Names for each year of account."
His comments came as Hiscox reported an increase in pre-tax profits to 14.3 million stg in 1996, up from 1.9 million stg the previous year.
Underwriting at Lloyd's contributed 6.2 million stg to the figures.

In July last year the company acquired the balance of shares in the managing agent of the Hiscox syndicates and the Economic Insurance Company, since renamed Hiscox Insurance company, funded by a 54.6 million stg rights issue.
Hiscox expects a profit from underwriting of between 8.7 million stg and 11.6 million stg in 1997.
The company is currently listed on the alternative investment market (AIM) but said last week it planned to join the full stock exchange in July.
By mid-morning the shares were unchanged at 135 pence.
